newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens bourse trade close to 3,200 pts.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens bourse trade close to 3,200 pts.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of leading shares on Monday opened bourse trade higher, close to the 3,200 points level, as the strong dollar marginally outweighed the negative impact of Wall Street's overnight losses.
The DAX-30 index rose 9.49 points to 3,193.85, while March DAX index up 12.5 points to 3,205.5, as the dollar traded firm at 1.666 marks and German debt futures were also higher.

"It's quite possible we'll get over 3,200 points today. The dollar's firm, and the view is that the problems among individual stock sectors in the U.S. need not necessarily have a bearing on German share values," said one dealer.

The dealer was referring to the sell-off in technology stocks that was largely responsible for the wider U.S. fall. The most obvious impact from the technology sell-off was seen in the shares of German software group SAP, down 2.50 marks at 253.50.
Volumes were widely seen as thin because of the half-day pre-Lent Karneval holiday in Frankfurt.

Drugs group Schering touched a new year-high of 147.20 in IBIS electronic trade after reporting better-than-expected net profit for 1996. It later dropped back to 144.20 marks, one mark up on the day, in early bourse trade.
